documents: Yang, Gomez, Schmid, Baringer 2022, Limnology and Oceanography Letters 7: 427-434 (published PDF)

entry.evidence: Net primary production (NPP) measurements in the open-ocean Gulf of Mexico are scarce and mostly limited to satellite-derived surface estimates.

steps.action: Frame the gap: depth-resolved, year-round NPP in the open-ocean GoM is unknown, because studies are coastal, satellite-surface-only, or limited to one season.
steps.quote: Field measurements of depth-resolved NPP in the open-ocean GoM are scarce and limited to a certain season

steps.action: Take from model studies the expectation that vertical mixing, lateral advection and mesoscale eddies drive seasonal variability of carbon production.
steps.quote: suggested that vertical mixing, lateral advection, and other mesoscale activities (e.g., Loop Current eddies) play important roles

steps.action: Adopt the published approach of adjusting uncalibrated float bio-optical data against satellite products to obtain a consistent dataset.
steps.quote: it is feasible to adjust the float measurements with satellite products

steps.action: Assemble 237 Chl and bbp profiles from four archived BOEM floats (2012-2015), compute MLD from density, and interpolate MODIS surface Chl, bbp and PAR to each profile.
steps.quote: A total of 237 profiles were used for this study

steps.action: Use a co-author's GoMBio model monthly DIN climatology, interpolated to float times and positions, as a stand-in for unmeasured nutrients.
steps.quote: we used the model outputs (monthly climatology from 2012 to 2014) from GoMBio (Gomez et al. 2018)

steps.action: Evaluate float Chl and bbp at about 8 m against satellite surface estimates: Chl correlates (R 0.65-0.76); bbp has the same magnitude but no significant linear relation (Fig. S1).
steps.quote: no significant linear relationship was found between them (Fig. S1a–d)

steps.action: Adjust the float Chl profiles with per-float type II regressions (Table 1) and leave bbp unadjusted to avoid artifacts.
steps.quote: the linear regression results shown in Table 1 were used to adjust the float Chl profiles

steps.action: Compute depth-resolved NPP with CbPM (bbp to Cphyto, Chl:C and light-based growth rate, PAR attenuation from Chl) and average into monthly climatologies of 17-22 profiles each; the choice is justified by the authors' earlier 14C agreement.
steps.quote: The carbon-based productivity model (CbPM; Behrenfeld et al. 2005, Westberry et al. 2008) was used to calculate the depth-resolved NPP

steps.action: Compare float surface NPP with satellite CbPM surface NPP for individual profiles (R 0.71) and monthly climatologies (R 0.94).
steps.quote: The adjusted float data yielded surface NPP values close to the satellite estimates (Fig. 2a)

steps.action: Compare the surface NPP seasonal cycle (winter high, summer low) with surface DIN and MLD, and with patterns reported in earlier satellite and model studies.
steps.quote: The seasonal pattern of surface NPP followed the seasonal variations of surface nitrate concentration (Fig. 3b)

steps.action: Attribute winter-high surface NPP to mixing-supplied nitrate, and offer photoacclimation as an additional factor for summer-low surface NPP.
steps.quote: The other factor that might play a role in summer low surface NPP is photoacclimation

steps.action: Estimate the 0-100 m integrated NPP seasonal cycle (maximum in May at over 500 mg m-2 d-1, minimum in December) and show it differs from the surface cycle (Fig. 3c).
steps.quote: Such seasonal variation is entirely different from the seasonal pattern of surface NPP

steps.action: Compare May integrated NPP and profile shape with 2017/2018 in situ shipboard estimates: values are higher, profile shapes are similar.
steps.quote: the shapes of depth profile were similar (Fig. 4a in this work vs. Fig. 2 in Stukel et al. 2021)

steps.action: Explain the absolute-value mismatch by auxiliaries (spatial and temporal mismatch, lack of shipboard calibration) rather than revising the estimates.
steps.quote: Possible explanations for the difference in the absolute NPP value includes the spatial/temporal mismatch of these two studies

steps.action: Compare monthly 0-20 m and 20-100 m integrated NPP with modelled DIN and PAR profiles (Fig. 4) to trace nutrient versus light control through the year.
steps.quote: From January to May, the NPP in the upper 20 m of the water column gradually decreased (Fig. 4a,b) due to the decreasing DIN

steps.action: Retain the layered control pattern: nutrients limit 0-20 m, light controls 20-100 m, and the deeper layer dominates the total except in December to February.
steps.quote: NPP in the surface layer (0–20 m) is mostly controlled by nutrient supply

steps.action: Propose lateral nutrient supply (river plume, Loop Current eddies) or lateral transport of organic matter for the July mid-depth NPP peak, untestable with the climatological DIN.
steps.quote: Alternatively, such high NPP signal at mid-depth could also be a result of the lateral transport of organic matter

steps.action: Keep the year-round depth-resolved NPP dataset as a tool for seasonal and vertical analysis, with absolute values flagged as uncertain.
steps.quote: Although there might be some uncertainties in the absolute NPP values due to the lack of shipboard field calibration

end.claim: Float-based, satellite-adjusted year-round depth-resolved NPP estimates show 0-100 m integrated NPP peaking in May while surface NPP peaks in winter, with the 20-100 m layer contributing more for most of the year.

decisive_move.sentence: Applying CbPM to the satellite-adjusted float Chl and unadjusted bbp profiles produced the depth-resolved NPP on which every claim rests.

gates.evidence: The floats were deployed by BOEM for a Lagrangian study of deep circulation, not to test an NPP hypothesis (p. 428). The surface NPP estimates faced a comparison with satellite NPP that could have failed (p. 430), but this comparison is not independent because float Chl was adjusted to satellite Chl. The control interpretations were posed after the data and not tested. Nothing is reported as fixed in advance.

imports.item: type II linear regression for float-satellite Chl adjustment

novelty_claims.quote: generating a consistent dataset for deriving the first year-round depth-resolved NPP estimates in this region
for the first time we obtained year-round in situ estimates of depth-resolved NPP in the historically understudied [...]

limits: Supplementary figures S1-S3 (the Chl/bbp evaluation, sampling distribution, July Chl/bbp) are cited but were not supplied, so the premise check is coded from the main-text summary. No review file was supplied; the paper was revised (submitted Oct 2021, revised Apr 2022), but the changes are unknown. Inference: the float-versus-satellite NPP comparison is circular in part, because float Chl was regressed onto satellite Chl and both NPP products use CbPM and satellite PAR. No sensitivity tests are reported for the CbPM parameters, the Graff Cphyto-bbp relation, the bbp spectral slope, the MLD criterion, or the leaving of bbp unadjusted. Why only four of the eight BOEM floats were used is not stated. Sub-claims: the layered nutrient-versus-light control and the winter mixing explanation are best_explanation (inferred from co-variation with a model DIN climatology, not tested). The July mid-depth peak mechanism is no_conclusion. The seasonal surface pattern is regularity_in_range (about 2012-2015, transitional open-ocean region). Inference: natures_repetition fits only loosely; the work is mainly an estimation from reused archived data with post hoc interpretation.

disagreements.support: Float-based May integrated NPP (about 42 mmol m-2 d-1) exceeds the shipboard 24-29 mmol m-2 d-1, while the profile shapes agree; the gap is attributed to spatial/temporal mismatch and lack of calibration.
disagreements.quote: was higher than the estimates (24–29 mmol m2 day1) from the April–May 2017/2018 in situ experiments

disagreements.target: Satellite-based surface NPP studies of the open-ocean GoM (e.g., Muller-Karger et al. 2015)
disagreements.support: The depth-integrated seasonal cycle differs entirely from the surface cycle, showing that surface-only estimates miss the water-column pattern.
disagreements.quote: [...] importance of obtaining depth-resolved NPP data for the studies of marine carbon production

disagreements.support: The modelled climatological DIN does not show the mid-depth nitrate increase implied by the July NPP peak.
disagreements.quote: the climatological DIN profiles from model outputs (Fig. 4c) could not reveal the increased mid- [...]

alternatives_considered.chosen: Low surface nitrate in a stratified mixed layer as cause of summer-low surface NPP
Lateral nutrient transport (Mississippi plume, Loop Current eddies) for the July mid-depth NPP peak
